children: NSE IPO anchor investors raised Rs 6,746 crore at Rs 1,785 per share, with LIC receiving the largest individual allocation ahead of the issue

The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has raised Rs 6,746.18 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), with Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) emerging as the largest individual investor in the anchor allocation. The exchange finalised the allocation of 3,77,93,739 equity shares at Rs 1,785 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band.
LIC Leads Anchor Allocation As NSE Raises Rs 6,746 Crore

LIC received 22,42,584 shares, representing 5.93 per cent of the total anchor allocation, valued at about Rs 400.30 crore. LIC is already NSE’s largest shareholder, with a 10.72 per cent stake in the exchange. Other prominent investors included Government Pension Fund Global, Monetary Authority of Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Fidelity-managed funds, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and several domestic mutual funds and insurance companies.

The anchor book drew participation from more than 150 institutional investors, with overseas funds accounting for about 43 per cent of the allocation. Foreign portfolio investors invested around Rs 2,883 crore, while domestic institutional investors also made a substantial contribution to the book. Domestic mutual funds accounted for 36.98 per cent of the total anchor allocation.

NSE said 13,977,524 shares were allotted to 29 domestic mutual funds through 98 schemes. Participating fund houses included SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Nippon India Mutual Fund, Kotak Mutual Fund, Axis Mutual Fund and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund.
Domestic, Global Investors Participate Ahead Of NSE IPO

Life insurance companies and pension funds were another major category in the anchor book. NSE said 6,060,744 shares, or 16.04 per cent of the total anchor allocation, were allotted to 27 life insurance companies and pension funds. Participants included SBI Life Insurance, HDFC Life Insurance, SBI Pension Funds, HDFC Pension Fund, Axis Max Life Insurance and UTI Pension Fund.

The exchange’s IPO is entirely an offer for sale (OFS), meaning the proceeds will go to existing shareholders selling their stakes rather than to NSE. The issue comprises up to 12.64 crore shares and has a price band of Rs 1,700 to Rs 1,785 per share. At the upper end of the price band, the issue size is about Rs 22,561 crore.

The IPO opens for public subscription on September 17 and closes on September 21. Share allotment is expected to be finalised on September 22, with NSE shares scheduled to list on September 24, subject to the proposed timeline. The anchor allocation comes after years of regulatory and procedural delays around NSE’s public listing. The participation of domestic mutual funds, insurers, pension funds and global institutional investors comes ahead of the exchange’s entry into the listed market.
